newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share index touch off in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share index touch off in active trade.

text.p: Nigerian shares finished steady in active dealing on Wednesday that cost some blue chips further ground, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 6654.53 from 6654.54 on Tuesday.
Lever Brothers and Cadbury, two highly capitalised companies were down on large sales, traders said. "Investors are just taking profit by selling their bonus shares," one said.
Lever Brothers went down by five kobo to 2525 naira and Cadbury was lower by the same margin at 25.90 naira.
Resurgent Nigerian Breweries rose 10 kobo to 10.60 naira, its third rise in as many days. "Investors think it is now cheap at the current level," said a trader.
Food companies Nestle and Union Dicon Salt were each ahead 30 kobo at 39.90 naira and 39.10 naira, respectively on positive investors' perception.
Nigerian Tobacco company was up three kobo at 3.21 naira.
West African Portland Cement ended 15 kobo up at 37.80 naira while construction firm G. Cappa closed up 25 kobo at 10.00 naira.

Demand for oil shares remained healthy. National Oil led the sector up, closing 22 kobo higher at 38.42 naira. Unipetrol was 46.32 naira, up 17 kobo, while African Petroleum notched 16 kobo to end at 36.36 naira.
Investors continued to offload shares of First Aluminium and Vitafoam, down seven kobo and five respectively at 4.30 naira and 3.40 naira.
Adjustment for dividend and scrip cost Cappa and D'Alberto a whopping 3.33 naira to close at 5.67 naira.
